# AI Workflow

## Project layout

Configured in `.ralph.env` (defaults shown; every generated script, skill, and
doc below honors these):

- Plan (PRD): `prd/PRD.md` — archived to `prd/archive/` when complete
- Issue files: `issues/`
- Manual-QA scenarios: `qa-manual-verification/`
- Verification contract: `./scripts/verify.sh` (stable wrapper; set the real
  checks inside it)
- Project context: `CONTEXT.md` (`RALPH_CONTEXT_FILE`) — the ONE agent-facing
  description of this project (folder map, which skill applies where, how to
  run things). Scaffolded as a suggestion at install; yours to edit, never
  overwritten. `ralph.sh` injects it into every developer/QA/planning prompt,
  so keep it current instead of repeating structure in prompts or docs.

This repo is configured for a provider-selectable AI workflow that turns an idea
into a PRD, splits the PRD into independently implementable issues, then lets
Ralph work through those issues one at a time with a separate QA Principal gate.

## Flow

1. Align on the design.

   Ask the configured developer agent to use the `grill-me` skill:

   ```sh
   grill me on this idea
   ```

   or, when the project has domain docs or needs terminology/ADR updates:

   ```sh
   use the grill-with-docs skill
   ```

2. Write the PRD.

   After the design is clear:

   ```sh
   use the write-prd skill
   ```

   This replaces the active PRD at `prd/PRD.md`.

   Then review the plan before building it:

   ```sh
   use the qa-review-plan skill
   ```

   Resolve any blockers it raises. This is the QA gate on the plan itself,
   separate from the per-issue QA that runs during Ralph.

   Optional multi-agent panel: `./ralph.sh --review-plan` reviews the PRD through
   several lenses (architecture, security, ops, testability), writes a consolidated
   `prd/plan-review.md` with a READY / NEEDS CHANGES verdict, and commits it. Enable it
   for remote runs with `PANEL_ENABLED=1` (`PANEL_BLOCKING=1` to stop before decompose
   on NEEDS CHANGES). See `.ralph.env` for the `PANEL_*` knobs.

   Plan scope gate (on by default): before `--decompose`, Ralph runs one agent call that
   judges whether `prd/PRD.md` is a single shippable slice. An over-scoped plan is
   hard-stopped *before* decomposition (no issues, no PR) with a suggested reduction in
   `prd/plan-scope.md`, so big features get split into multiple sequential plans — each
   shippable on its own, later slices kept dark behind a feature flag — and every run
   stays a limited, reviewable slice. `qa-review-plan` checks the same thing earlier and
   for free. Set `PLAN_SCOPE_GATE=0` to skip it.

3. Split the PRD into issues.

   Ask the developer agent to use the `prd-to-issues` skill.

   This creates one markdown file per task under `issues/`, named like
   `001-short-slug.md`.

4. Review the issues.

   Before running Ralph, check that the issue files are small, ordered, and have
   clear acceptance criteria. Each issue should be a vertical slice that can be
   implemented, tested, committed, and closed independently.

5. Run Ralph.

   Commit the workflow plan first, then start from a clean worktree:

   ```sh
   git add prd/PRD.md issues/*.md
   git commit -m "plan AI workflow issues"
   git status
   ./ralph.sh
   ```

   Ralph invokes the configured developer CLI in headless mode. Each iteration
   picks one issue, asks the developer agent to implement and verify it, then
   Ralph commits the work, removes the issue file, commits that closure, and
   repeats until there are no issues left or a safety stop is hit.

   The `issues/` directory must be trackable by Git. Do not exclude it in
   `.gitignore`; Ralph removes completed issue files with `git rm`.

## Remote mode (hand off to GitHub Actions)

Instead of running Ralph locally, hand an approved plan off to GitHub Actions,
which decomposes it, runs the same dev/QA loop, archives the PRD, and opens a PR.

1. Write and review the plan (steps 1-2 above: `write-prd`, then `qa-review-plan`).
   Do NOT run `prd-to-issues` — the remote run decomposes the plan itself.
2. Hand off the plan:

   ```sh
   ./ralph-handoff.sh my-feature
   ```

   This creates a `ralph/my-feature` branch, commits `prd/PRD.md` (plus any
   `CONTEXT.md`/`docs/adr` updates from `grill-with-docs`), and pushes it.
3. The push triggers `.github/workflows/ralph-remote.yml`, which opens a tracking
   issue (label `ralph:run`), runs `ralph-remote.sh` (decompose -> dev/QA loop ->
   archive PRD -> push), and opens a PR. Follow progress on the tracking issue.
4. Review the PR; your normal PR checks run on it. Merge when happy (which closes
   the tracking issue).

Setup (once per repo): add the repository secrets.

- **Claude auth — pick one.** Subscription (recommended): run `claude setup-token`
  (Claude Pro/Max) and store the `sk-ant-oat01-...` token as
  `RALPH_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; runs bill your subscription instead of
  pay-per-token API credit. Long autonomous loops can exhaust Pro-plan rate limits —
  Max is the comfortable tier. Or metered: set `RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (needs a
  funded console.anthropic.com balance). If both exist the run prefers the
  subscription token and drops the API key; an unset secret is never exported as
  an empty variable.
- **Codex auth (only if an agent is `codex`).** Codex runs on your ChatGPT
  subscription via its `auth.json`, not an OpenAI API key (the API-key path bills
  the metered account and fails with "Quota exceeded" without credits). Run
  `codex login` locally — on a headless/remote machine, `codex login
  --device-auth` — then: `gh secret set RALPH_CODEX_AUTH_JSON < ~/.codex/auth.json`.
  The runner seeds `~/.codex/auth.json` from that secret and Codex refreshes the
  token itself. (`RALPH_OPENAI_API_KEY` is still honored as a legacy fallback.)
- **`RALPH_GH_TOKEN`** — a PAT or GitHub App token with
  contents/issues/pull-requests write plus actions read (the idempotency gate
  lists workflow runs), so the auto-opened PR triggers your PR workflows.

The installer offers to store all of these via `gh secret set` at the end of
setup, and `setup-ai-workflow.sh --doctor` re-checks which secrets are present
for the agents configured in `.ralph.env`.

Remote runs use the claude developer
agent with bypassPermissions inside the ephemeral runner. The generated workflow
pins the Claude Code CLI install and only exposes secrets to the GitHub/agent
steps that need them. A failed or cancelled run does not block the branch: to
retry, push a new commit or re-run the workflow from the Actions tab (the
`force` input bypasses the idempotency gate; a `[ralph force]` commit trailer
does too). New pushes are only skipped while another run for the branch is
actually in progress or queued, when the pushed commit is no longer the branch
tip (a stale queued event), or when the push is Ralph's own (a `[ralph skip]`
marker or a `ralph-bot` committer) — completed issues are pushed as they close,
and those persistence pushes must not spawn duplicate runs.

**Recovery after a failed run.** Nothing is lost and nothing blocks:

- Issues that already passed QA are committed and pushed the moment they close,
  so cancellation, a timeout, or a lost runner cannot discard them; a retry
  detects the existing decomposition and resumes the loop directly instead of
  re-planning.
- A cancelled or timed-out run also preserves the attempt that was in flight:
  an always() workflow step commits the dirty work under the recorded issue
  identity and pushes it before the runner disappears.
- If the run died after the whole plan completed but before the PR was opened,
  a retry recognizes the archived plan on the branch and simply opens the PR —
  no agents run and no agent credentials are required.
- If an issue exhausted its QA budget, its work-in-progress is preserved on the
  branch as a `wip(<issue>)` commit whose body carries the accumulated QA
  findings, and the tracking-issue comment lists those findings plus the
  remaining issues. Push a commit addressing the findings: the run re-triggers,
  resumes that issue on top of the WIP with a fresh QA budget (your push counts
  as the developer round), and continues.
- The run report and QA findings are also uploaded as a workflow artifact.
- The tracking issue is closed (reason: not planned) on failure and reopened by
  the retry, so a slug's whole story stays in one thread.

### Remote verify contract (CI runner setup)

Remote runs execute `scripts/verify.sh` on a **clean `ubuntu-latest` runner** that
starts with only Node and the Claude CLI. Anything else your verification needs —
language runtimes, package managers, a database, a headless browser — must be
installed by the workflow, or verify fails on the runner and no PR is opened. This
is the contract: `scripts/verify.sh` must pass using *only* what the workflow
provisions.

So before your first hand-off, edit the CI-setup regions in
`.github/workflows/ralph-remote.yml` (and mirror them in `.github/workflows/verify.yml`,
the PR check) to provision your stack. There are two preserved regions:

- **Steps** — between the `RALPH-CI-SETUP-BEGIN` / `RALPH-CI-SETUP-END` marker
  lines: install runtimes and tools, start services via Docker, etc.
- **Job-level config** — between the `RALPH-CI-JOB-SETUP-BEGIN` /
  `RALPH-CI-JOB-SETUP-END` marker lines: keys that cannot live between steps,
  such as `services:`, job `env:`, or `container:`.

Keep the marker lines: re-running the installer refreshes the rest of the
workflow to the latest template while preserving everything between them —
job-level config placed OUTSIDE the marked regions is not part of the template
and only survives upgrades on a best-effort basis. In `ralph-remote.yml`, gate
every step you add with `if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'`. Docker and
Docker Compose are preinstalled on the runner.

Don't want to write the YAML by hand? Paste this prompt to a coding agent (claude,
codex, ...) **from inside your repo** and let it generate the steps:

> Configure this repository so its automated verification passes on a clean GitHub
> Actions `ubuntu-latest` runner. Both `.github/workflows/ralph-remote.yml` and
> `.github/workflows/verify.yml` run `scripts/verify.sh` as the gate, and the runner
> starts with only Node and the Claude CLI installed.
>
> 1. Read `scripts/verify.sh` and every command it invokes. List each language
>    runtime, package manager, CLI tool, and service (database, cache, broker,
>    headless browser, ...) it depends on.
> 2. Pin versions from the repo: `.python-version`, `.nvmrc`, `.tool-versions`,
>    `pyproject.toml` (`requires-python`), `package.json` engines, lockfiles,
>    Dockerfiles, and any `docker-compose*.yml`.
> 3. In `.github/workflows/ralph-remote.yml`, replace the content BETWEEN the
>    `RALPH-CI-SETUP-BEGIN` and `RALPH-CI-SETUP-END` marker lines (keep both
>    markers) with steps that install those runtimes/tools and start those
>    services. Gate EVERY added step with `if: steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'`.
>    Docker and Docker Compose are preinstalled; if verify needs services, start
>    them here and wait until they are healthy.
> 4. Any JOB-LEVEL keys you need (`services:`, job `env:`, `container:`, ...)
>    go BETWEEN the `RALPH-CI-JOB-SETUP-BEGIN` and `RALPH-CI-JOB-SETUP-END`
>    marker lines (keep both markers) — never outside the marked regions, or a
>    template upgrade may drop them.
> 5. Put the same steps and job-level config (without the `if:` gate) in
>    `.github/workflows/verify.yml` so the PR check matches.
> 6. Do not weaken or skip any check in `scripts/verify.sh`. If a check cannot run on
>    CI, make verify.sh provision what it needs rather than removing it. Read any
>    service credentials from workflow `env`/secrets and keep secrets out of logs.
> 7. Re-read both workflows and confirm that, from a bare `ubuntu-latest`, every
>    command in `scripts/verify.sh` has its dependency satisfied. Summarize what you
>    added and why.

Projects scaffolded by `create-project.sh` already ship this block filled in for
their FastAPI + Next.js + Playwright stack, so they run remotely out of the box.

## Manual QA verification pass

Separate from Ralph's automated final gate, three skills drive a manual
human-in-the-loop QA loop over `qa-manual-verification/`. This pass is run by
hand, and the handoff from QA to development is deliberately manual.

1. Catalog the flows. Ask the QA agent to use the `qa-identify-scenarios` skill.

   It enumerates the product's user-facing flows and reconciles them against the
   `qa-manual-verification/NNN-*.md` scenario files, creating any that are
   missing. It only adds gaps; it never renumbers or rewrites existing scenarios.

2. Walk the scenarios and log findings. As you (or the QA agent) step through
   each scenario, use the `qa-feedback` skill to record every finding into
   `qa-manual-verification/999-qa-feedback.md` as a finding card plus a row in
   the global register, each starting at status `open`.

3. Hand off to development (manual). Once the findings are identified, you decide
   when to act on them and ask the developer agent to use the `qa-address-issues`
   skill. Nothing advances automatically.

4. Address the open findings. The developer agent works the `open` rows one at a
   time: `open -> in review -> confirmed`, reproduces the finding in the local
   stack, fixes it with TDD, then stops for your QA review before you let it move
   the finding to `resolved`. You own the gate into `resolved`.

These skills are installed for both the developer and QA agents, so either
provider can run its part of the chain.

## Ralph Configuration

Override these with environment variables:

```sh
VERIFY_CMD="./scripts/verify.sh" ./ralph.sh
ALLOW_DOCKER=1 ./ralph.sh
DEVELOPER_AGENT=codex QA_AGENT=gemini ./ralph.sh
DEVELOPER_MODEL="" QA_MODEL="" ./ralph.sh
MAX_ITERATIONS=5 ./ralph.sh
RALPH_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600 ./ralph.sh
PERMISSION_MODE=default ./ralph.sh
CODEX_SANDBOX=danger-full-access ./ralph.sh
CODEX_DEVELOPER_REASONING_EFFORT=medium ./ralph.sh
CODEX_QA_REASONING_EFFORT=high ./ralph.sh
CLAUDE_DEVELOPER_EFFORT=medium ./ralph.sh
CLAUDE_QA_EFFORT=high ./ralph.sh
MAX_QA_FIXES=3 ./ralph.sh
QA_DIFF_MAX_BYTES=900000 ./ralph.sh
QA_FULL_REVIEW_ROUNDS=2 ./ralph.sh
```

Defaults:

- `DEVELOPER_AGENT=claude`
- `QA_AGENT=gemini`
- `DEVELOPER_MODEL=""` and `QA_MODEL=""`, which lets each CLI use its current
  default/latest model
- `PERMISSION_MODE=acceptEdits`
- `MAX_ITERATIONS=20`
- `RALPH_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600`, so each developer, QA, and QA-fix CLI
  call has a one-hour timeout instead of being able to hang the unattended loop
- `MAX_QA_FIXES=3`, so with the default `QA_FULL_REVIEW_ROUNDS=2` each issue gets
  two comprehensive discovery reviews then up to two scoped verification rounds
  (four reviews, three automatic developer fix attempts) before Ralph stops for
  manual review
- `QA_DIFF_MAX_BYTES=900000`, so a large single-issue diff is truncated before
  it reaches provider CLI input limits
- `QA_FULL_REVIEW_ROUNDS=2`, so the first two QA reviews of an issue are full
  comprehensive (discovery) passes before re-reviews switch to scoped, delta-only
  verification that confirms fixes and flags regressions without re-litigating
  pre-existing code
- `VERIFY_CMD=./scripts/verify.sh`
- `CODEX_SANDBOX=danger-full-access`, applied to EVERY codex invocation
  (developer, QA reviewer, QA fix, panel), so Codex runs can execute the repo
  verification contract and inspect the repo when they need local resources
  such as Docker
- `CODEX_DEVELOPER_REASONING_EFFORT=medium`, used for Codex implementation and
  QA fix runs
- `CODEX_QA_REASONING_EFFORT=high`, used for Codex QA review runs
- `CODEX_PLANNING_REASONING_EFFORT=high`, documented for manual Codex planning,
  PRD, and issue-creation sessions
- `CLAUDE_DEVELOPER_EFFORT=medium`, used for Claude implementation and
  QA fix runs
- `CLAUDE_QA_EFFORT=high`, used for Claude QA review runs
- `CLAUDE_PLANNING_EFFORT=high`, documented for manual Claude planning, PRD,
  and issue-creation sessions
- Gemini CLI does not currently expose a reasoning-effort flag in this workflow;
  use `GEMINI_*_MODEL`-equivalent model selection through `DEVELOPER_MODEL` and
  `QA_MODEL` when Gemini needs a stronger planning or QA model.
- `ALLOW_DOCKER=auto`, which notes when verification scripts or compose files
  indicate Docker may be used by the verification contract
- Ralph allows developer agents to run read-only inspection commands such as
  `pwd`, `ls`, `find`, `rg`, `sed`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, and read-only
  Git commands so they can understand the issue and codebase.
- Tests, type checks, lint, migrations, package-manager commands, Docker
  commands, and network installs must not be run directly by developer agents.
  Put every required check behind `scripts/verify.sh`.

`DEVELOPER_AGENT` and `QA_AGENT` must be different (`claude`, `gemini`, or
`codex`). If `VERIFY_CMD` is unset or blank, Ralph falls back to
`./scripts/verify.sh` rather than inspecting the project and guessing how tests
should run.

### Verification contract

Every configured project gets `scripts/verify.sh`. Treat that script as the
single repo-owned command that decides whether Ralph may commit.

For simple projects it might just run `npm test`. For real projects, especially
monorepos and mixed stacks, it should run every required check across Python
workers, Node frontends, API services, database migrations, infrastructure, and
smoke tests. If verification needs containers, put the required Docker or
Docker Compose orchestration in this script. It may delegate to `make verify`,
`just verify`, `task verify`, or any other local task runner.

The script should be deterministic and require no network installs. If the
project needs targeted module checks, put that routing logic inside
`scripts/verify.sh` rather than relying on Ralph to infer every technology
boundary. Ralph supports Docker-based verification through the verification
contract; it does not ask the developer agent to run direct Docker commands
outside that contract. Set `ALLOW_DOCKER=1` to always disclose that Docker may
be used by verification, `ALLOW_DOCKER=0` to suppress that disclosure, or keep
the default `auto`.

Developer agents may use read-only inspection commands to understand the issue
and repository, including `pwd`, `ls`, `find`, `rg`, `sed`, `cat`, `head`,
`tail`, `wc`, `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git rev-parse`, and
`git branch`. Any tests, type checks, lint, migrations, package-manager
commands, Docker commands, or network installs needed for verification must run
through `scripts/verify.sh`.

### Persistent config: `.ralph.env`

The setup script writes `.ralph.env` in the repo root. Ralph sources it on
startup, so anything you set there is picked up automatically. Edit it any
time to change settings persistently — no need to re-run setup. Example:

```sh
# .ralph.env
DEVELOPER_AGENT=codex
QA_AGENT=gemini
DEVELOPER_MODEL=''
QA_MODEL=''
VERIFY_CMD='./scripts/verify.sh'
RALPH_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=3600
CODEX_SANDBOX=danger-full-access
CODEX_DEVELOPER_REASONING_EFFORT=medium
CODEX_QA_REASONING_EFFORT=high
CODEX_PLANNING_REASONING_EFFORT=high
CLAUDE_DEVELOPER_EFFORT=medium
CLAUDE_QA_EFFORT=high
CLAUDE_PLANNING_EFFORT=high
ALLOW_DOCKER=auto
MAX_QA_FIXES=3
QA_DIFF_MAX_BYTES=900000
```

For manual planning, PRD, and issue-creation work, start the chosen provider
with its high-effort option when the CLI supports one:

```sh
codex -c model_reasoning_effort=high
claude --effort high
```

`QA_CMD` is an advanced override. Leave it empty to use `QA_AGENT` and
`QA_MODEL`. If set, it must read the diff on stdin and end with `PASS` or
`FAIL: <reason>`.

### QA review (per issue, before each commit)

Ralph runs the QA Principal **once per issue**, after the developer's work for
that issue passes the verification contract and before Ralph commits it. On
stdin the reviewer gets the issue spec (its acceptance criteria) followed by only
that issue's diff (`git diff <pre-issue HEAD>` plus untracked files), not a
whole-plan cumulative diff. The issue spec lets QA confirm the diff actually
implements the selected issue, and it is read from the **pre-issue baseline**
(not the worktree), so an agent that edits `issues/*.md` before QA cannot change
the criteria QA judges against. This keeps every review small, focused, and cheap,
and it means a finding is raised against the change that introduced it. Ralph
expects the output to end with a line starting with `PASS` or `FAIL: <reason>`.

The whole reviewer payload is strictly capped by `QA_DIFF_MAX_BYTES` (default:
`900000`). On truncation Ralph emits, in priority order and each capped to the
remaining budget: a truncation notice, the issue context (spec, prior findings,
delta), the `git diff --stat` file list, then the diff body. The diff body is the
first to be dropped; the issue context is only ever truncated as a last resort
when it alone would exceed the cap. Either way the total stdin never exceeds the
cap, so it cannot blow past provider input limits. Generated lockfiles are
omitted from the diff body; keep dependency intent in manifest files such as
`package.json` or `pyproject.toml`.

QA reports its findings in a structured, machine-parsed block — numbered, with
severity, `file:line`, and the required fix — before its PASS/FAIL verdict, and
every round is APPENDED to a findings history. If QA fails, Ralph sends the
developer that accumulated history (never just the last round) plus the fenced
issue spec, asks it to fix the blockers for **that issue only**, run the
verification contract, leave the fixes unstaged, and answer every numbered
finding with a `FINDING <n>: FIXED — ...` or `FINDING <n>: DISPUTED — ...`
line; the next review receives those answers as untrusted claims to verify.
Ralph then re-reviews the same issue in one of two modes. The
first `QA_FULL_REVIEW_ROUNDS` reviews (default `2`, counting the initial review)
are **discovery** rounds: the reviewer sees the issue spec and the full issue diff
and — from the second round on — its previous findings to confirm resolved, and it
may still raise any blocker. That gives QA two comprehensive passes to find
everything before the scope closes. After the discovery window, re-reviews go
**scoped**: the reviewer is handed its previous findings and a delta of exactly
what the developer changed since the last review (computed by diffing snapshot
trees, so newly added files are included; bounded by `QA_DIFF_MAX_BYTES`, and if
truncated the reviewer gets the two tree IDs plus the exact `git diff <prev> <cur>`
command to reconstruct the full scoped delta). The full issue diff is deliberately
left out of scoped rounds, so the reviewer cannot keep re-discovering pre-existing
code and burning retries; it confirms each finding is resolved and flags only new
bugs or regressions in the delta, reconstructing surrounding context with `git`
only if it needs it. Scoped re-review only kicks in after a genuine `FAIL` verdict;
if the previous round was a reviewer infrastructure failure (CLI/API error or a
missing verdict), the next round is a full discovery review again, so a transient
outage never lets unreviewed changes slip through. By default Ralph allows three
automatic developer fix attempts per issue (`MAX_QA_FIXES`), which with
`QA_FULL_REVIEW_ROUNDS=2` is two discovery rounds then two scoped rounds; raise it
for more scoped verification rounds. If an issue exhausts its attempts, Ralph
stops for manual review with that issue's changes still uncommitted.

Verdicts:

- `PASS` line in the last 10 lines → Ralph commits the issue and moves on.
- `FAIL` line in the last 10 lines → Ralph records the failure and either
  starts a bounded developer fix attempt or stops after the retry limit.
- No explicit `PASS` line (missing or malformed verdict) → treated as `FAIL`,
  and the next round falls back to a full discovery review.
- Reviewer command exits non-zero → treated as `FAIL`, with the same
  discovery-review fallback next round.

On a stop, inspect with `git status` and `git diff`. The failing issue's changes
stay uncommitted and its issue file stays in `issues/`; you can amend, revert, or
clarify the issue file, then re-run Ralph from a clean tree. Earlier issues that
already passed QA are committed and unaffected. Ralph never rewrites history.

This QA gate is **separate** from verification. Tests / type-check run inside
each developer iteration via the verification contract; the QA reviewer only
sees a diff of work that already passed those checks.

When the last issue passes its QA gate and `issues/` is empty, Ralph runs one
**final whole-plan QA audit** before archiving. Each issue passed its own gate in
isolation, so this pass is a cross-issue integration and completeness check: the
reviewer gets the PRD acceptance criteria, the QA notes carried across the plan
(each issue can append a `NOTES FOR FINAL REVIEW:` section on PASS), and the
whole-plan file list, with repository read access to inspect the integrated
result. It should normally find nothing. On `PASS` Ralph archives the active PRD
by moving `prd/PRD.md` to `prd/archive/<timestamp>-PRD.md` and committing that
move, then clears the carried QA notes. On `FAIL` it leaves `prd/PRD.md` active
and stops for manual review instead of declaring the plan complete. Ralph only
reaches this point when it actually completed at least one issue: if `issues/` is
already empty when Ralph starts (for example a PRD was written but `prd-to-issues`
has not run yet), it leaves `prd/PRD.md` untouched instead of archiving an
unstarted plan.

The reviewer CLI is invoked from `ralph.sh` directly, outside the developer
agent context, so issue text cannot steer it. If a reviewer (a QA agent or
`QA_CMD`) writes to the worktree while returning `PASS`, Ralph detects that the
tree no longer matches the reviewed diff and refuses to commit the unreviewed
changes, stopping for manual review instead.

Ralph makes its own commits with `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit`, which
disables **all** git hooks (not just `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` like `--no-verify`,
but also `prepare-commit-msg` and `post-commit`). So no hook can modify or stage
extra files into a reviewed commit — or into the follow-up close commit — after QA
has approved the diff; what lands always equals what was reviewed. Put project
checks in the verification contract (`scripts/verify.sh`), not in git hooks.

## Safety Rules

Ralph is intentionally conservative:

- It requires a clean Git worktree before each iteration.
- It stops if the developer agent leaves uncommitted changes behind.
- It stops if the developer agent commits its own work (HEAD moves off the
  pre-issue baseline), since that would bypass the per-issue QA gate.
- It stops if any agent modifies files under `issues/` (the selected spec, or
  another issue added/edited/deleted), so a future issue can never be silently
  dropped and the PRD archived as complete; Ralph alone removes the selected
  issue, after QA.
- It uses a lock in Git's internal directory to prevent two Ralph runs from racing.
- When Claude is the developer, it uses a narrow Claude Code tool allowlist for
  Git and verification commands.
- It stops after `MAX_ITERATIONS`.
- It stops a per-issue QA remediation after `MAX_QA_FIXES` automatic developer
  fix attempts.
- It stops after two consecutive iterations with no visible progress.

`./ralph.sh --unsafe-bypass` enables Claude Code `bypassPermissions`, but it
refuses to run unless `CLAUDECODE_SANDBOX=1` is set. Only use that inside an
isolated container or VM with no internet access.

## Recovering From Stops

If Ralph stops:

1. Run `git status`.
2. Inspect any uncommitted changes.
3. Either finish and commit them manually, or revert/stash them deliberately.
4. Fix the issue file if the task was unclear. If this was a per-issue QA
   failure after the retry limit, the failing issue's changes are still
   uncommitted and its issue file is still present; amend, revert, or clarify the
   issue, then re-run Ralph from a clean tree to retry just that issue.
5. Re-run `./ralph.sh` from a clean worktree.

If Ralph reports that its lock already exists and no Ralph process is running,
remove it:

```sh
rmdir "$(git rev-parse --git-path ralph.lock)"
```

A per-issue QA cycle keeps no QA baseline between runs: Ralph reviews each issue's
own diff and resets its per-issue scratch files (`ralph.qa-failures`,
`ralph.qa-last-review`, `ralph.qa-prev-tree`, `ralph.qa-last-was-real`) at the
start of every issue. One marker *does* persist across runs: `ralph.plan-active`,
set once Ralph closes an issue of the current plan and removed when the PRD is
archived; it lets a later rerun archive a completed plan even if the prior run
stopped right after the final issue. To abandon a stuck issue, revert or stash
its uncommitted changes (and optionally edit or remove its issue file), then
re-run Ralph from a clean tree. To abandon a whole plan without archiving its
PRD, also remove `$(git rev-parse --git-path ralph.plan-active)`.

## Generated Files

Managed generated files include an `AI-WORKFLOW-MANAGED` marker. Re-running
setup refreshes marked files and writes a timestamped `.bak.*` copy before
replacing changed content. Existing unmarked files are left alone unless you pass
`--force`, which also creates a backup before replacement.

- One developer instruction file: `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, or `AGENTS.md`
- One QA Principal instruction file for a different provider
- Provider-specific engineering skills:
  - Claude: `.claude/skills/{api,python,frontend}/`
  - Gemini: `.gemini/skills/{api,python,frontend}/`
  - Codex: `.agents/skills/{api,python,frontend}/`
- Provider-specific workflow skills for the developer agent:
  - Claude: `.claude/skills/`
  - Gemini: `.gemini/skills/`
  - Codex: `.agents/skills/`
- Plan and manual QA skills, installed for both the developer and QA agents:
  - `qa-review-plan/` (review the PRD before hand-off)
  - `qa-identify-scenarios/`, `qa-feedback/`, `qa-address-issues/`
- `prd/`
- `issues/`
- `scripts/verify.sh`
- `ralph.sh`
- `ralph-handoff.sh` (remote mode: push an approved plan to a `ralph/<slug>` branch)
- `ralph-remote.sh` (remote mode: GitHub Actions orchestration)
- `.github/workflows/ralph-remote.yml` (remote mode trigger; created once, then customize)
- `.github/workflows/verify.yml` (CI: runs scripts/verify.sh on push/PR; created once, then customize)
- `.ralph.env`
- `AI-WORKFLOW.md`

## Observability

Each run prints an end-of-run summary (status, issues closed/stopped, per-issue
developer/QA time and QA rounds) and writes it to `.git/ralph-run-last.md`.

For live updates, point `RALPH_PROGRESS_HOOK` at an executable; Ralph calls it as
`hook <event> [slug]` for these events: `run-start`, `decomposed`, `issue-started`,
`issue-closed`, `issue-failed`, `plan-complete`, `run-stopped` (slug carries the status
on `run-stopped`). Example notifiers:

```sh
# Slack incoming webhook
#!/bin/sh
curl -fsS -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"text\":\"ralph: $1 $2\"}" "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" >/dev/null

# macOS desktop notification
#!/bin/sh
osascript -e "display notification \"$1 $2\" with title \"ralph\""

# terminal bell when a run stops
#!/bin/sh
[ "$1" = run-stopped ] && printf '\a'
```

Set `RALPH_PROGRESS_HOOK=/path/to/notify.sh` in `.ralph.env` to enable it.
